# Base data fields (per installed dataset)

Reference **only** fields available in the dataset your loop runs on — availability differs by market (e.g. `cn_data` has `$change`, `us_data` does not; neither has `$vwap`). Prefix each with `$` in expressions.


| field | note | `cn_data` | `us_data` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$change` | daily change | yes | — |
| `$close` | close price (adjusted) | yes | yes |
| `$factor` | adjustment factor | yes | yes |
| `$high` | high | yes | yes |
| `$low` | low | yes | yes |
| `$open` | open price (adjusted) | yes | yes |
| `$volume` | volume | yes | yes |

## ⚠️ On `cn_data`: DO NOT USE `$vwap`

Alpha158/Alpha360 reference `$vwap`, but `cn_data` does **not** contain it; any feature using `$vwap` resolves to NaN and silently degrades the model. Avoid.


## ⚠️ On `us_data`: DO NOT USE `$vwap`

Alpha158/Alpha360 reference `$vwap`, but `us_data` does **not** contain it; any feature using `$vwap` resolves to NaN and silently degrades the model. Avoid.


## Label convention (from the qlib templates)

The prediction label is the 2-day-ahead forward return: `Ref($close, -2)/Ref($close, -1) - 1`. Because the label horizon is 2 days, any leakage-safe CV must embargo >= 2 days (ADR 0001 §7 v1).
